Disclosure  to  Promote  the  Right  To  Information 

Whereas  the  Parliament  of  India  has  set  out  to  provide  a  practical  regime  of  right  to 
information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public. 


Mazdoor  Kisan  Shakti  Sangathan 
"The  Right  to  Information,  The  Right  to  Live''

RECOMMENDATIONS  FOR 
HEAT   EXCHANGER  GASKETS 


(  Reaffirmed  1999) 


1.  Scope  —  Covers  the  design,  material,  shape,  constrtrction  and  other  details  of  different  type  of 
heat  exchanger  gaskets. 

2.  Materials  —  Heat    exchanger  gaskets    generally  shall    be   made    out    of    single    material    or 
composite  materials  to  suit  the  specific  application  and  service  condrtion. 

The    following   shall    be    the    general    materia!    out    of    which    heat  exchanger    gaskets   are 
manufactured: 


a)  Soft  iron/carbon  steel  conforming  to  IS  :  4030-1 973 
'Cold  rolled  carbon  steel  strip  for  general  engineer- 
ing purposes  (  first  revision  )' 

b)  Admiralty  brass  conforming  to  IS  :  410-1977  'Cold 
rolled  brass  sheet,  strip  and  foil  ( ttiird  revision  )' 

c)  Copper  conforming  to  IS  :  8362-1977  'Copper  and 
copper  alloy  rolled  plates  for  condensers  and  heat 
exchangers' 

d)  Aluminium  conforming  to  IS  :  737-1974 'Wrought 
aluminium  and  aluminium  alloys  and  strip  for  general 
engineering  purposes  (  second  revision  )' 

e)  Monel  conforming  to  IS  :  4131-1967  'Nickel  copper 
alloy  casting' 

f)  Brass  conforming  to  IS  :  8362-1977 

g)  Stainless  steel  conforming  to  IS  :  6911-1972  'Stain- 
less steel  plate  sheet  and  strip' 

h)  Compressed  asbestos  conforming  to  IS  :  2712-1979 
'Compressed  asbestos  fibre  jointings  ( second 
revision  )' 

j)  SS  jacketed  asbestos 

k)  Soft  iron  jacketed  asbestos 

m)  Monel  jacketed  asbestos 

n)  Brass  jacketed  asbestos 

p)  Copper  jacketed  asbestos 

q)  Aluminium  jacketed  asbestos 


Hardness,  Max,  90  BHN 

Soft  annealed 

Soft  annealed  80  BHN 

Soft  annealed 

Soft  annealed  140  BHN 

Soft  annealed  80  BHN 
Hardness,  Max,  140  BHN 


Hardness,  Max,  140  BHN 
Hardness,  Max,  90  BHN 
Soft  annealed  140  BHN 
Soft  annealed  80  BHN 
Soft  annealed  80  BHN 
Soft  annealed 


Any  other  material  may  be  used  as  agreed  to  between  the  manufacturer  and  the  purchaser. 


3.  Construction 

3.1   Heat  exchanger  gaskets  shall  be  made  in  one  piece  as  shown  in  Fig.  1. 
gaskets  made  integral  by  welding.

GASKET 

3.2  Complete  gasket  including  all  ribs  and  each  lamination  of  gaskets  shall  be  cut  from  a  single 
sheet. 

3.2,1   If  the  size  of  the  gasket  exceeds  the  commercially  available  metal  or  material,  proper  joint- 
ing is  permitted. 

3.3  Heat  exchanger  gaskets  of  jacketed  type  are  made  by  cladding  the  ^oft  filler  material,  like 
asbestos  either  partially  or  wholly  with  a  stronger  supporting  metal.  The  following  thicknesses  of 
the  filler  material  shall  be  used  for  these  gaskets: 

0*6  mm 

10  mm 

V6  mm 

3'15  mm,  and 

4  mm. 

Unless  otherwise  specified  by  the  purchaser,  the  soft  filler  material  shall  be  asbestos  of  good 
quality  chrysotiie. 

3.4  Metal  used  in  the  jacketed  gaskets  exceeds  the  size  of  the  commercially  avarlable  metal  sheet 
joints  are  permitted. 

3.4.1  Joints  in  the  jacketed  gasket  shall  be  made  by  butt-welding  the  edges. 

3.4.2  Excess  metal  in  the  joint  shall   be  removed  and  the  thickness  at  the  joint  shall  be  the  same 
as  adjacent  metal- 
There  shall  be  150  mm  gap  between  the  joints  in  the  opposite  faces  of  the  jacketed  gasket. 

4.  Design  —  The  jacketed  material  thickness  shall  be  0"375  mm  minimum  and  0*5  mm  maximum. 

4.1  The  filler  material  thickness  shall  be  V5  mm  minimum. 

4.2  Unless  otherwise  specified  by  the  purchaser,  the  closing  lip  of  the  folding  shall  be  2'5  mm 
minimum  and  the  fillet  radii  shall  be  10  mm. 


IS  :  10864-1984 

5.  Dimensions  and  Tolerances 

5.1  Dimensions — Heat  exchanger  gaskets  are  always  custom-built  which  necessarily  demands  the 
purchaser  to  provide  the  details  of  material,  shape  and  size  and  the  dimensions  of  the  gaskets  clearly. 

Wherever  orientation  of  the  gasket  with  respect  to  the  flange  seating  is  preferred,  it  shall  be 
clearly  mentioned  in  the  drawing  provided  by  the  purchaser, 

5.2  Tolerance  —  Unless  otherwise  specified  by  the  purchaser,  the   following  dimensional  tolerances 
shall  be  followed  for  all  types  of  heat  exchanger  gaskets; 

a)  OD  of  the  gasket  ±  0'8  mm 

b)  ID  of  the  gasket  ±  0     mm 

c)  Position  of  the  pass  partition  rib  ±  08  mm 

d)  Width  of  the  rib  '  +0     mm 

~  0*8  mm 

e)  Thrckness  of  the  gasket  +  0'35  mm 

—  0     mm 

6.  Shipment 

6.1  Gaskets  shall  be  properly  protected  from  rust  and  other  surface  damage. 

6.2  Gaskets  shall  be  properly  packed  and  protected  from  distortion  and  damage  while  in  transit. 

6.3  Gaskets   shall    be   tagged   or   marked   with   the    symbol   and   other  drawing  numbers    for  easy 
identification. 


EXPLANATORY     NOTE 

Since  heat  exchangers  gaskets  are  needed  for  all  joints  in  contact  with  oil  or  oil  vapour,  the 
material  and  dimensions  of  the  gaskets  have  to  be  carefully  selected.
